card.statement:
The scheme $\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}$ is denoted $\mathbb{S}^{\mu}$ in [10, §2.5], and the open subscheme ${}_{0}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}$ is denoted ${}_{0}\mathbb{S}^{\mu}$. The scheme $\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}$ is denoted $\mathfrak{F}^{-\mu}$ in [17, §3.6.3], and the open subscheme ${}_{0}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}$ is denoted $\mathring{\mathfrak{F}}^{-\mu}$.

We continue with our closed point $c\in C$, and consider the affine Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_{c}$ for the group $G$, defined as in §2.7 but with respect to the completion of the local ring of $C$ at $c$. (For any choice of a local coordinate at $c$ this completion identifies with $\mathbb{F}(\hskip-1.0pt(z)\hskip-1.0pt)$, which provides an identification of $\mathrm{Gr}_{c}$ with $\mathrm{Gr}$; but the definition can be phrased without any choice of coordinate, which is what we mean by $\mathrm{Gr}_{c}$.) We have therein the semi-infinite orbits $\mathrm{S}_{\lambda,c}$ and $\mathrm{S}^{-}_{\lambda,c}$ ( $\lambda\in\mathbf{Y}$ ) defined using the action of the loop groups of $U$ and $U^{-}$ respectively. By [10, Proposition 2.6], there exists a canonical isomorphism

${}_{0}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}\cong\mathrm{S}_{\mu,c}\cap\mathrm{S}^{-}_{0,c}.$

This isomorphism is roughly defined as follows. An $\mathbb{F}$ -point in the left-hand side is a triple $(\mu\cdot c,\mathcal{E},\beta)$ where $\mathcal{E}$ is $G$ -torsor on $C$ and $\beta$ is a trivialization over $C\smallsetminus\{c\}$, subject to the conditions from (4.6) and (4.7). The maps $\kappa_{\xi}$ and $\tau_{\xi}$ from (4.7) define a $B^{-}$ -reduction and a $B$ -reduction, respectively, of $\mathcal{E}$. That is, we get a $B^{-}$ -torsor $\mathcal{G}^{-}$ and a $B$ -torsor $\mathcal{G}$. These torsors inherit the trivialization $\beta$ away from $c$, so we get points in $\mathrm{Gr}_{B^{-}}$ and in $\mathrm{Gr}_{B}$. By examining the domain of $\kappa_{\xi}$ and the codomain of $\tau_{\xi}$, we find that $\mathcal{G}^{-}$ must lie in $\mathrm{S}^{-}_{0,c}\subset\mathrm{Gr}_{B^{-}}$, and $\mathcal{G}$ in $\mathrm{S}_{\mu,c}\subset\mathrm{Gr}_{B}$.

From this identification and standard facts about semiinfinite orbits (see e.g. [6, Proposition 3.9]) we deduce that

$\dim(\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c})=\langle\mu,\rho\rangle.$

On the other hand, it is explained in [17, §3.6.3] that we have a canonical identification

(4.30)

$\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}\cong\overline{\mathrm{S}_{0,c}}\cap\mathrm{S}^{-}_{-\mu,c}$

which restricts to an identification

(4.31)

${}_{0}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}\cong\mathrm{S}_{0,c}\cap\mathrm{S}^{-}_{-\mu,c}.$

4.11. Smoothness
card.label: Remark 4.17

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
